steps.title: Assign temporary extraction numbers
steps.instruction: Renumber all lab lichen samples consecutively using the prefix X for lichens (e.g., X001, X002, …). Record each number in the lab book, on a sampling slip attached to the specimen packet, in the EDNA_submissions_sheet_211209.xlsx, the EDNA database, and the RBGE DToL barcoding Google sheet. Avoid placing samples from the same genus or species in consecutive tubes.

steps.title: Acetone rinse of lichen fragments
steps.instruction: Process ~3 mm² of clean lichen material (thinly slice apothecia if present) to reduce secondary compounds.

substeps.instruction: Place the lichen fragment(s) in a 1.7 mL tube.
Add approximately 50 µL acetone so the tissue is completely covered; soak for at least 30 min.
Pipette the acetone into a labelled 500 µL tube.
Leave both the lichen tube and the acetone tube open in a fume hood to air‑dry (≈10 min for the lichen tube; 30 min–1 h for the acetone tube).
After drying, either send the acetone tube for thin‑layer chromatography or store it with the herbarium specimen for possible future TLC.

steps.title: REDExtract‑N‑Amp DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the acetone‑rinsed lichen using REDExtract‑N‑Amp Plant PCR kit reagents (≈1/3 reaction volumes).

substeps.instruction: Aliquot REDExtract‑N‑Amp extraction and dilution reagents into 1.5 mL tubes; store at –20 °C.
Preheat a heat block to 95 °C (≈20 min) and defrost the aliquoted extraction and dilution solutions.
Add about 30 µL extraction solution to each lichen sample so the tissue is fully covered.
Vortex briefly, spin down, and verify that the tissue is well submerged (extra agitation may be needed for hydrophobic material).
Incubate the tube for 10 min at 95 °C, watching the lids for possible opening.
Add 30 µL dilution solution (same volume as extraction buffer) to neutralize inhibitors.
Store the extracted DNA at 4 °C until further use.
Bank the DNA stock by pipetting the supernatant (avoiding lichen debris) into barcoded tubes; long‑term storage can be at –20 °C or lower.

steps.title: Dilute DNA stock for PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare working DNA dilutions for downstream PCR and sequencing.

substeps.instruction: For standard samples, mix 3 µL DNA stock with 27 µL molecular‑grade water (1:10 dilution) in a PCR strip.
For very scant samples, mix 3 µL DNA stock with 12 µL water (1:5 dilution).

steps.title: Bento dipstick DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from microlichens (<1 mm² to 3 mm²) using the Bento Dipstick kit, producing a DNA stock for later PCR.

substeps.instruction: Place the tiny lichen fragment directly into a 1.7 mL tube.
Add a pinch of sterilised sand and 20–40 µL extraction buffer; homogenise with a micro‑pestle.
Add extraction buffer incrementally until the total volume reaches ~300 µL (up to 500 µL if needed); homogenise as required.
Prepare a wash‑buffer tube for the sample: 750 µL wash buffer in a 1.7 mL tube (use 500 µL for very small samples).
Prepare 25 µL TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA) in a labelled 0.5 mL tube for the DNA stock.
Arrange two dipsticks per sample on clean paper or foil.
For each dipstick:
a. Dip the cellulose end into the DNA/extraction buffer three times to bind DNA.
b. Dip into the wash buffer three times, pressing the cellulose end against the tube wall to expel excess wash.
c. Dip into the TE buffer for about 10 seconds, gently agitating to release DNA and form the stock.
d. Repeat steps a–c with the second dipstick.
Spin down the eluted DNA and store at –20 °C for long‑term or at 4 °C for immediate use.
For maximal yield, incubate dipsticks in TE buffer as long as possible, stopping just before the cellulose end detaches; if it breaks, remove the end with a pipette tip.
Crude DNA extracts may be frozen, then gently defrosted and warmed in a water bath for future use (not yet experimentally validated).

steps.title: Store frozen lichen material
steps.instruction: Maintain frozen lichen specimens and any remaining thallus for future work.

substeps.instruction: Keep frozen samples in clearly labelled batches; limit exposure to room temperature to the brief period needed for DNA extraction.
After successful sequencing of a batch, forward the frozen specimens together with the DToL manifest and EDNA accession numbers to herbarium staff for long‑term curation.
If any thallus remains after extraction, return the tube to the freezer drawer.
Occasionally, preserve fresh lichens in TE buffer and freeze them for later DNA extraction.

steps.title: Long‑term DNA banking
steps.instruction: Archive high‑quality barcode DNA for future reference.

substeps.instruction: Store barcoding DNA short‑term in labelled 1.7 mL elution tubes at 4 °C.
Arrange DToL tubes taxonomically in 96‑sample racks using the temporary extraction numbers (A, F, B, L, X).
When all samples in a rack have yielded good barcode sequences, transfer the DNA, preserving the same order, into barcoded fluidX tubes placed in 96‑tube racks.
Scan the tube and plate barcodes and store the racks at –80 °C.
Enter all tube and plate barcode details into the RBGE DNA database (EDNA).

steps.title: Direct PCR for problematic specimens
steps.instruction: Perform PCR directly on tiny or contaminated lichen material without prior DNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 0.2 mL tube containing 20 µL PCR mix for each specimen (duplicate tubes are recommended).
Under a stereo microscope, use sterilised blades or needles to cut sections of the target tissue (e.g., apothecia or perithecia).
Place the sections on a slide and, at higher magnification, dissect to isolate the desired part (e.g., hymenium only).

Using a sterile pipette tip or needle moistened with sterile water or PCR mix, pick up a minute piece of the target tissue and transfer it into the PCR tube, confirming placement under the microscope.
Run the PCR as per the chosen protocol.
